depth.rationale: The hard part is real and original. It covers an anisotropic time-dependent Dijkstra with a hand-written heap and an Anderson ellipse (pipeline/ember/spread.py), a two-stage inversion with a hinge loss and a per-fit shape cap (s11_ignition.py), synthetic-case calibration checked out of sample, a timing gate, forensic perimeter cleaning (s05), hand-implemented Mantel-Haenszel/RBG and IRLS statistics (s09b), and server-side checks on LLM paragraphs (web/api/_lib/verify.ts). The formulas are published and the code is hand-rolled, not copied (grep for copied/adapted/Source found nothing relevant). Share estimate: about 2,000 lines of original logic (the files named in the advisor list, less their I/O) out of about 14,200 non-blank source lines, roughly 14% of the total and about a quarter of the non-UI code. Glue and I/O: the s01-s04 and s07-s09 fetch and reprojection code, tools.ts accessors, and about 6,300 lines of web UI. Split on the pending analyst (README.md:40, not yet run live): I credit verify.ts and analyst.ts as original logic because web/api/_tests (verify.test.ts, loop.test.ts) exists. I do not credit end-to-end analyst behaviour. The loop itself (analyst.ts:91-142) is a standard function-calling pattern and gets only glue-plus credit. Withheld: the headline Eaton fit, its hold-out and its synthetic benchmark all run with the cap at 1.0, so the ellipse and wind direction are inert there. This is disclosed (README.md:71), but the anisotropic physics does little on the headline fire. The 'posterior' is a re-weighting of two non-uniform candidate sets, and the Palisades hold-out temperature falls back to a ceiling. Constants are unsourced, and the analyst's number checks and eval scorer are loose. I ran no tests or evals (read-only), and the tests named here were not run. Score 8 rather than 9 because of the inert ellipse and the heuristic uncertainty. It would be 9 if the Eaton ellipse were active and calibration never fell back.

judge.rationale:
Verdict: reject. Rule 1 fails on its own: the fixed arithmetic gives 72.5 weighted + 2 bonus = 74.5, below 80. Rule 2 holds: zero critical findings survived, and after checking all ten adversary findings against the repo I agree none is critical. Every headline number reproduces, the real-fire failures are disclosed, and what remains is overstatement plus a reproduce-path defect. With my own scores substituted (works 7.5, evidence 6, clarity 7) the total would be about 74, so the gap is real, not an artefact of one agent.

What I verified myself (read-only on the judged checkout; runs from a scratchpad copy using the runner's venv, writing only to the scratchpad):
- Tests: 136 passed, 6 skipped in 21.7 s on the committed outputs for both fires (same counts as the runner).
- Reproduction, which the runner could not check this round because its EVAL_DIR path contained a space: the QUICK check reproduced both synthetic cases identically to eval/ignition_synthetic.json (cases_checked 2, identical True; 8 min 21 s, longer than the README's "about 6 min" at README.md:171), and the full real Eaton hold-out rerun matched the committed eval/ignition_holdout.json in all 57 fields (11 min 8 s). So README.md:170-171 are true claims; adversary F4 is a path-quoting defect, not a reproducibility failure. Root cause is in two places the team controls: pipeline/Makefile:63 and :66 expand EVAL_DIR unquoted (confirmed with make -n: "EVAL_DIR=/tmp/a b FIRE= uv run ..."), and the repo's own harness docs/judge/judge-round.js:116 and :118 pass EVAL_DIR=${wt.run}/../eval-out-run, which on this machine lives under "Application Support". The next round fails the same way unless one of them changes.
- The web app, which no agent rendered this round: I served the runner's web/dist and opened ?fire=eaton and ?fire=palisades in a browser. Both load their own committed files: 3D terrain with the stylized texture, interpolated progression driven by the timeline (Eaton 5,994 ac at Jan 8 10:50 PST; Palisades 16,885 ac), mapped perimeter at t, dNBR scar, ignition posterior with "Start time withheld: 90% start-time interval is 9.9 h wide (limit 6 h)" for Eaton and the 22.3 h plus k-at-ceiling reasons for Palisades, charts, key events, weather at t, and a map key tagging REAL/MODELED. No console errors except my static server's 501 on POST /api/analyst; the Analyst tab showed "The analyst returned HTTP 501." and nothing canned. This matches README.md:41 and the panel's code reading.
- Adversary F1 (confirmed, major): the Eaton seed in arrival_meta.json is 1,744 m from CAL FIRE's reported point, snapped into the first footprint by s06_arrival.py:78-79, yet labelled "CAL FIRE official start and reported location" (s06:70) and described at README.md:54 as seeded from the reported location. Palisades is 7 m, so only Eaton is affected.
- Adversary F2 (confirmed, major): the Palisades hold-out estimate is 2025-01-09T10:27:04Z, after both held-out perimeters (2025-01-08T20:34Z and 21:24Z), with predicted_cells 0 and IoU 0.00 for both; README.md:120 shows "40.0 h (-707.9 h)" as a baseline comparison without saying the estimate post-dates the observations it is scored against.
- Adversary F3 (replayed): with score_fit stubbed and the committed seed, my replay regenerates the same 30 truths per fire and finds the true origin inside the first fitted footprint in 30/30 Eaton cases (both scenarios), 30/30 Palisades hold-out cases and 29/30 Palisades all-observation cases (one is 95 m outside). The adversary reported 26/30 and 29/30; the direction is confirmed and stronger. This is not rigging, since a synthetic fire grown from its origin naturally contains it, but it is a benchmark-scope gap: the real Eaton reference sits 1,772 m outside the search domain (README.md:133), and README.md:152 lists only perturbations as the calibration-scope caveat.
- Panel evidence point (a) (confirmed): README.md:86 says the synthetic k range "is not set from a real fit", but commit 0eab9dc set K_TRUE_RANGE to (4, 16) "Eaton-like fast fires ... the real Eaton fit needs k ~ 11", and 66e8516 moved it to (0.25, 4) in the same commit that moved the real Eaton fit to k 0.42 under HRRR. The current range contains the real Eaton k (0.424) and excludes the real Palisades k (22.6 hold-out, 76.8 full; synthetic truths 0.33-3.6), so the Palisades 100%/100% coverage row is measured outside its real regime.
- Adversary F6 is misclassified: BUILD.md:182's 46 mph and r 0.67 match comparison_era5_seamless (ERA5 at the fire-area point) in the same weather_station.json; RESULTS.md:143 quotes comparison_era5_seamless_at_station (47 mph, 0.71). Two unlabelled comparisons, both in the cited file. Wording, not major.
